short: Edward VI was King of England and Ireland from 1547 until his death, overseeing the establishment of Protestantism.
full:
Edward VI, the long-awaited male heir of Henry VIII, inherited the throne at the age of nine. His reign was governed by a Regency Council, first led by his uncle Edward Seymour and later by John Dudley. Though young, Edward took a keen interest in religious matters, and his reign saw the Church of England transform into a fully Protestant body, sweeping away clerical celibacy and the Mass.

In 1553, Edward fell fatally ill. Attempting to prevent a Catholic restoration, he drew up a "Devise for the Succession" that bypassed his half-sisters Mary and Elizabeth in favour of his cousin Lady Jane Grey. His death at fifteen triggered a succession crisis; Jane reigned for just nine days before Mary gathered overwhelming support, took the throne, and rapidly reversed Edward's religious reforms.
